re_line: Trump-Xi summit outcomes, Taiwan arms package on hold, Second Thomas Shoal standoff, AI rivalry, China's stimulus push
editors_note: This is the first China Room Brief. It arrives every Friday with the week in U.S.-China relations and what CSIS scholars have coming.

week_at_a_glance.headline: Golden Week ends as refiners await export approvals
week_at_a_glance.body: China's seven-day National Day holiday concludes on October 7. Traders are watching whether Beijing resumes approvals for refiners' fuel exports suspended for the break, after Reuters reported PetroChina cancelled a small number of planned gasoline and jet-fuel cargoes on September 30.

week_at_a_glance.headline: PBOC runs 1.2 trillion yuan reverse repo
week_at_a_glance.body: A 1.2 trillion yuan three-month buyout reverse repo operation is set for October 8, Reuters reported, part of a package with a nationwide mortgage-interest subsidy effective October 1. Analysts told Bloomberg the measures will likely secure Beijing's GDP target but deliver little additional lift.

week_at_a_glance.headline: IMF and World Bank meet in Bangkok
week_at_a_glance.body: The IMF/World Bank Annual Meetings run October 12 to 18 in Bangkok. China's growth trajectory and debt-related concerns typically feature prominently.

week_at_a_glance.headline: Bloomberg New Economy Forum opens in New Delhi
week_at_a_glance.body: From October 13 to 15, the New Delhi forum carries an explicit "levers of power" framing amid U.S.-China-India triangulation.

heard_on_the_hill.headline: Senate puts off Chinese car ban until after midterms
heard_on_the_hill.body: The Senate punted a bill that would permanently ban Chinese-made cars from the U.S. market until after the November 3 midterm elections, AP reported. Reuters reported senators plan to bring the measure up again for a vote in November. Separately, Sen. Moreno told CNBC a bill he sponsors to bar companies with more than 15 percent Chinese ownership from selling vehicles in the U.S. would not affect Mercedes-Benz.

heard_on_the_hill.headline: Wicker says U.S. must honor Taiwan commitments
heard_on_the_hill.body: Senate Armed Services Committee Chairman Roger Wicker said U.S. security commitments to Taiwan must be upheld after meeting Taiwan's representative Alexander Yui, the Taipei Times reported. Four other Republican senators called on the administration to release more than $14 billion in stalled Taiwan security assistance. House Speaker Mike Johnson dismissed suggestions the delayed package is being used as leverage in trade talks.

heard_on_the_hill.headline: Senate bill would bar Chinese optical modules
heard_on_the_hill.body: A bipartisan Senate group proposed banning Chinese-made optical modules from federal national-security systems, with a five-year grace period. Chinese chip and optical stocks slid to a one-year low on the news, Bloomberg reported, with ChiNext down 4.53 percent.

heard_on_the_hill.headline: Lawmakers move to keep Chinese datacenter gear out
heard_on_the_hill.body: Members of Congress are moving to keep Chinese-origin datacenter hardware and software out of sensitive U.S. government systems, Reuters reported, following warnings that Chinese AI models and cloud infrastructure could pose data-security risks to federal networks.

heard_on_the_hill.headline: Republican chair seeks scrutiny of Seoul's China ties
heard_on_the_hill.body: A Republican committee chair called for greater scrutiny of South Korea's ties with China, according to a brief Reuters dispatch that gave no specific findings or proposed actions.

in_the_news.headline: Divisions between US and China 'simmer beneath the surface' after Xi's Washington visit
in_the_news.body: Xi Jinping's September 23-25 state visit yielded tariff relief on $30 billion of goods each way, a November AI dialogue, a two-month truce extension and a Chinese pledge to buy at least 10 million metric tons of U.S. coal in each of 2027 and 2028. Xi pressed Trump to "oppose" Taiwan independence. Export controls, AI and Taiwan arms sales went unaddressed in public readouts, the New York Times reported.

in_the_news.headline: Philippines accuses China of obstructing resupply mission
in_the_news.body: Manila said China blocked a September 24 resupply mission to its grounded vessel at Second Thomas Shoal, the first such incident since 2024, per Bloomberg reporting cited by HKEJ. The U.S. embassy in Manila accused Beijing of "dangerous blocking and irresponsible manoeuvres," while China Coast Guard spokesperson Jiang Lüe said Manila "broke its promise."

in_the_news.headline: DeepSeek and Huawei unveil AI chip tools to rival Nvidia's software stack
in_the_news.body: DeepSeek and Huawei jointly developed software tools for advanced AI chips, aiming to give Chinese developers an alternative to Nvidia's dominant chip-software ecosystem, the New York Times reported. The push is part of Beijing's AI self-reliance drive following U.S. restrictions on Nvidia's most advanced chips.

in_the_news.event: Chinese hackers impersonate U.S. AI insiders
in_the_news.headline: Suspected Chinese hackers impersonated US AI insiders
in_the_news.body: Suspected Chinese hackers impersonated an Anthropic employee and former U.S. officials to extract insights on American AI development, a U.S. cybersecurity firm told CNN. Reuters separately reported they posed as a former official to steal emails from AI experts.

in_the_news.headline: Analysts: China's 'mini stimulus' secures growth target, not much more
in_the_news.body: The PBOC, Ministry of Finance and financial regulator rolled out a nationwide mortgage-interest subsidy effective October 1, a cut to the Pledged Supplementary Lending rate and a 1.2 trillion yuan reverse repo set for October 8. A State Council meeting showed leaders "worried about economic performance for the rest of the year," per Sinocism. Analysts told Bloomberg the package secures the growth target and little more.

research_roundup.headline: The Limits of Trump and Xi’s Photo-Op Summit
research_roundup.body: David Sacks of CFR finds Trump and Xi reached no consensus on major geopolitical issues, made no headway on regulating AI and did not put economic ties on a more sustainable trajectory, calling the visit "a new high-water mark for symbolism and a new low for substance." He adds that it was not "a complete failure."

research_roundup.headline: The Trump-Xi Summit Leaves Taiwan in Limbo
research_roundup.body: CNAS argues public accounts of the summit show no U.S. agreement to Xi's push to move Washington closer to Beijing's position on Taiwan. Whether Trump can keep negotiating with Xi "while making Taiwan harder to conquer" is now the measure of his cross-Strait policy.

research_roundup.headline: How do we deal with Chinese overcapacity?
research_roundup.body: Cecilia Malmström, Yeling Tan, Alicia García-Herrero and Nicolas Lamp take up Chinese overcapacity after a summit that reached no agreement on it, noting that an EU-China working group on "macroeconomic imbalances" set up in May has failed to produce results so far.

research_roundup.headline: The PRC’s Compute Push Goes Global
research_roundup.body: Dennis Yang finds Beijing pushing its domestic computing ecosystem overseas before the compute crunch caused by U.S. export controls on high-end GPUs is resolved, citing calls for "compute going global" and a Shenzhen AI action plan released in early September.

research_roundup.headline: Return of Tensions in the South China Sea Was a Matter of Time
research_roundup.body: Andrew Chubb of the Asia Society Policy Institute's Center for China Analysis argues that after two years of relative quiet, China-Philippines clashes were all but inevitable. The most serious came on July 20, when Chinese Coast Guard personnel and Philippine marines fought with batons and paddles near Second Thomas Shoal.

qa: Week at a Glance items dated from news reports, not the calendar (confirm the date): "PBOC runs 1.2 trillion yuan reverse repo".
In the News outlets: New York Times, Reuters, New York Times, CNN, Bloomberg. 3 of 5 from NYT, WSJ, Washington Post, Bloomberg or FT.
Heard on the Hill cites taipeitimes.com, not a primary record or priority outlet: "Wicker says U.S. must honor Taiwan commitments".
"Reported" two or more times in 1 item(s), first: "Senate puts off Chinese car ban until after midterms".
